subject: german
title: Stamp 3: Parties and the Chancellor
welcome_lead: Stamp the German party landscape and the office of Chancellor.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on CDU, SPD, Grune, FDP, AfD, and the office of Bundeskanzler.

concepts.def: Federal Chancellor; head of government, currently Friedrich Merz (CDU).
Christian Democrats; centre-right alliance (CSU only in Bavaria).
Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands; centre-left, oldest German party (founded 1863).
Green party; environmental and socially progressive.
Freie Demokratische Partei; liberal party emphasising free markets.
The Left; successor to the PDS (former SED), strong in eastern Germany.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Bundeskanzler sets policy guidelines (Richtlinienkompetenz) and chairs the cabinet. The Bundestag elects the chancellor by absolute majority and can only remove them via a constructive vote of no confidence.
Helmut Kohl (CDU, 1982-98), Gerhard Schroder (SPD, 1998-2005), Angela Merkel (CDU, 2005-21), Olaf Scholz (SPD, 2021-25), Friedrich Merz (CDU, from 2025).

The constructive vote of no confidence requires the Bundestag to elect a new chancellor at the same time as removing the incumbent. It prevents Weimar-style power vacuums. Successful only in 1982 (Kohl replacing Schmidt).
